classification.difficultyReason: Proves an exact definite integral using tangent addition and the range of the resulting angle.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\int_{-\frac14}^{\frac35}\frac{1}{1+x^2}\,dx&=\left[\tan^{-1}x\right]_{-\frac14}^{\frac35}\\&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac35\right)-\tan^{-1}\left(-\frac14\right)\\&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac35\right)+\tan^{-1}\left(\frac14\right).\end{aligned}$$
Let $A=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac35\right)$ and $B=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac14\right)$. Using the tangent addition identity,
$$\begin{aligned}\tan(A+B)&=\frac{\tan A+\tan B}{1-\tan A\tan B}\\&=\frac{\frac35+\frac14}{1-\frac3{20}}\\&=\frac{\frac{17}{20}}{\frac{17}{20}}\\&=1.\end{aligned}$$
Since $0<A<\frac\pi4$ and $0<B<\frac\pi4$, we have $0<A+B<\frac\pi2$. Therefore $A+B=\frac\pi4$, so
$$\int_{-\frac14}^{\frac35}\frac{1}{1+x^2}\,dx=\frac\pi4.$$
